set.body:
After the typed core is stable, add an optional JVM/app-level EngineCatalog for dynamic plugin discovery. Shared code remains statically typed; string names from CLI/config resolve at the edge into typed plugin packages.

Acceptance: built-ins can be inspected like fmrireg engine_specs without exposing mutable registries; third-party interpreters can be supplied explicitly; unresolved names fail during preflight; no dynamic loading leaks into shared core.

Sequential assessment 2026-09-12: retain P3 deferred; not a current core defect. Current FitInterpreters.forEngine exhaustively matches the closed FitEngine enum. FitInterpreter is a public trait, but that alone does not prove a new third-party engine can traverse plan construction, preflight, dispatch and result handling. No EngineCatalog or ServiceLoader-based plugin implementation was found in module Scala sources, and this issue names no concrete external interpreter or application requirement. The parent architecture umbrella is now retired.

Activation trigger: an actual separately maintained interpreter and consuming application require extension beyond existing built-ins. First establish the typed registration/configuration/preparation/result contract and prove that explicit registration works through the public executor. Do not start with runtime discovery or weaken FitEngine/scientific result identity merely to fit a string registry. Keep built-in introspection, explicit third-party registration and optional JVM dynamic discovery as distinct acceptance steps; discovery is justified only if the consumer needs it.

Retain original safety requirements: unresolved names fail at the application boundary before work; shared JVM/JS core has no mutable global registry or dynamic loading. Any future implementation must demonstrate the concrete consumer path and both-platform built-in behavior. Current assessment does not claim custom engines or plugins are supported.
set.title: [DEFERRED] Define a typed external-engine contract before optional plugin discovery
